html:
King of the Maya city of Palenque, in what is now Chiapas, Mexico, from 615 to 683. He came to the throne at 12, after his mother Sak K'uk' held power, and ruled for 68 years.

Palenque had been sacked twice by its powerful rival Calakmul shortly before his reign. Pakal rebuilt it. He enlarged the Palace and gave the city the elegant style it is known for.

His tomb lies deep inside the Temple of the Inscriptions. Archaeologist Alberto Ruz Lhuillier found it in 1952. Pakal lay under a carved stone lid with a jade mosaic mask on his face. The lid shows him at the root of the world tree, between death and rebirth.

The temple's long texts in Maya script, dated with the Long Count, tell his ancestry and deeds. That makes him one of the best documented Maya rulers. His son K'inich Kan Bahlam II finished the temple.
